fieldValues.title: Retire 7 ext:* subsection husks: Protocol, Import-tracking, Themes, Lifecycle, Views-l1/l2, Repository (RFC-042 Change B, srs#710)
fieldValues.summary: Finished deleting 7 already-split subsection husks under rfc-decision-1e7c0c8e: fixed 72 mechanism successors missing meta.derivedFrom, reparented 41 orphaned example leaves to their concept parents, repointed one stale RFC manifest token, and spliced one precedes gap. Found and fixed a new class of drift: relation create doesn't sync Part-container membership across a Part boundary.
fieldValues.body:
Claimed 2026-09-11T~12:30Z from srs#710's gate:dispatched via srs#580's queue. Ground re-measured current state on a freshly unshallowed worktree matching origin/master (a93c4c5): 1 section (Key Invariants) and 20 subsections remained, matching the prior dispatch's own count exactly.

Selected the 7 subsections whose content already read "Content relocated to mechanism leaves under the ... concept ... See derived-from" -- meaning an earlier batch had already created their successors but never actually deleted the husk: ext:protocol, ext:import-tracking, ext:themes-l1, ext:lifecycle, ext:views-l1, ext:views-l2, ext:repository.

For each of the 72 mechanism successors (linked via a derived-from relation to its husk), checked meta.derivedFrom and found none set -- provenance existed only as the relation, which record delete --cascade destroys along with the deleted target (carried-context-a2429c55). Set meta.derivedFrom on all 72 via record update before deleting anything.

For each husk's remaining outbound contains children (4-9 example leaves per husk, 41 total), matched each to its sibling mechanism by title ("The X shape" <-> `X`) and found the correct target concept via the mechanism's own contains-parent (carried-context-87e8e448's orphaned-example pattern). Added the missing contains edge from the concept to each orphan before deleting the husk.

Grepped every RFC's srs-integration manifest for a section:/subsection: token citing any of the 7 husks' title slugs (carried-context-c4e43a58): one hit, rfc-48838a46 (RFC-027) citing subsection:ext-views-l2. Identified the correct successor by content match (the mechanism titled `RelationsPresentation` (RFC-027), the only one of ext:views-l2's 15 successors naming that RFC) and repointed the manifest token to mechanism:relationspresentation-rfc-027 via record update.

Checked the ext:* shadow-record fallback (carried-context-4c6e0ddc) for ext:protocol and ext:repository, the two of the 7 without a com.semanticops.spec/extension shadow record: grepped every RFC manifest for either token as a bare srs-integration line and found none, so no shadow record was needed before deleting either.

Traced the local precedes chain for all 7 husks: ext:lifecycle -> ext:protocol -> (external successor) formed a headless 2-node span needing no splice; the other 5 were individually chain terminals on at least one side. ext:views-l2 alone had both a live predecessor (387ca99d) and a live successor (78fecb62) outside the batch, so spliced 387ca99d -> 78fecb62 directly after its deletion.

Deleted all 7 with record delete --cascade; each call's cascadedRelations count reconciled exactly against a relation map built beforehand (accounting for the one precedes edge shared between ext:lifecycle and ext:protocol, counted once, in the first delete).

Ran part-container-membership.mjs and found the Extensions Part container still declared the 7 deleted husks' now-orphaned descendants as members even after the CLI's own auto-remove-on-delete handled the 7 husks themselves. Fixed the Extensions container with srs container members remove for the 41 stale ids -- but that only restored Extensions to match; it revealed a second-order problem. Running validate-all.mjs (real exit code, not through tail) showed 4 OTHER Part containers (Distribution, Structure, Foundations, Presentation) now drifted, computed-larger-than-declared by exactly 41 combined. Initially misdiagnosed this as pre-existing drift via a git stash comparison against the prior commit -- but git stash without -u does not stash untracked files, and the 41 new relation files this unit's own reparenting created were untracked, so that comparison was contaminated by the very change it was supposed to isolate. A true pristine `git clone` at the exact same prior commit (a93c4c5), confirmed independently by that commit's own green GitHub Actions Validate run, showed all 9 Part containers matching with zero drift -- proving the 4-container drift was entirely this unit's own reparenting, not pre-existing. Walked manifest.json's Part anchors to find which Part's contains-subtree actually reaches each of the 6 target concepts (Protocol -> Structure; Import-tracking, Repository -> Distribution; Lifecycle -> Foundations; Theme, View -> Presentation) and added each reparented id to the correct Part container via srs container members add. part-container-membership.mjs --check then reported all 9 Parts matching, and validate-all.mjs's real exit code went from 1 to 0.

check-release-drift.mjs correctly failed on the stale rendered docs before re-render (expected, per the Rendered Outputs procedure), then passed clean after node scripts/publish-spec.mjs with the pinned CLI (v0.1.0-build.376).

Running tally under rfc-decision-1e7c0c8e: #744 (7) - #745 (6) - #747 (2) - #749 (5) - #752 (9) - #755 (5) - #756 (11) - this unit/PR #758 (7) = 52/75 retired. Remaining: Key Invariants (1 section, blocked on carried-context-31ea3659) and 13 subsections.

PR: https://github.com/the-greenman/srs/pull/758, gate:auto-merge armed (SQUASH). Stopping per the merge-rights contract.

New carried_context filed (related below) for the Part-container membership gap -- the first batch in this series whose reparenting crossed a Part boundary, so no prior unit had occasion to find it.
